content: 1. Verapamil levels or effects may be increased by itraconazole due to inhibition of CYP3A4 metabolism. This can lead to toxicity, including peripheral edema, dizziness, hypotension, flushing, and headache. Consider reducing the verapamil dose or discontinuing one of the agents. Alternatively, avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Itraconazole increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can raise vilazodone plasma levels by 50%. Reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily when coadministered with itraconazole. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Itraconazole increases vorapaxar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Itraconazole increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Both itraconazole and ziprasidone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Itraconazole increases abemaciclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients starting on 150 or 200 mg BID of abemaciclib, reduce the dose to 100 mg BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If the dose has already been reduced to 100 mg BID due to adverse reactions, further reduce to 50 mg BID. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the abemaciclib dose to the pre-inhibitor level after 3-5 half-lives of the inhibitor. 7. Both albuterol and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Itraconazole increases alfentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Itraconazole increases alosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Aluminum hydroxide decreases itraconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. 11. Itraconazole increases amitriptyline levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Both itraconazole and amitriptyline prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Itraconazole increases amlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) have negative inotropic effects that may be additive with itraconazole. Monitor for adverse reactions, and dose reduction of the concomitant drug may be necessary. 13. Itraconazole increases apalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Itraconazole increases apixaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein metabolism. For patients on 5 or 10 mg BID of apixaban, reduce the dose by 50% when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors. Avoid coadministration in patients on 5 mg BID. 15. Both apomorphine and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Both arformoterol and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Itraconazole increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual aripiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the aripiprazole dose. 18. Itraconazole increases armodafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Both arsenic trioxide and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both agents prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Itraconazole increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Itraconazole increases atevirdine levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Itraconazole increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The recommended atogepant dose is 10 mg PO daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Both atomoxetine and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Both azithromycin and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Itraconazole increases bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Belzutifan decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate as per prescribing information. 28. Itraconazole increases benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. 29. Itraconazole increases berotralstat levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Itraconazole increases betrixaban levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg PO once, then 40 mg PO daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 31. Itraconazole increases bexarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Itraconazole increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Itraconazole increases bosentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while bosentan decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Itraconazole increases brentuximab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. 35. Itraconazole increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 36. Itraconazole increases buprenorphine subdermal implant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 37. Itraconazole increases buprenorphine long-acting injection levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels and signs of toxicity. If toxicity occurs and the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. 38. Itraconazole increases buspirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased buspirone effects or toxicities when combined with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 39. Itraconazole increases busulfan levels by decreasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Itraconazole increases calcifediol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 41. Calcium carbonate decreases itraconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. 42. Itraconazole increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 43. Itraconazole increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Itraconazole increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Refer to the dosage modification section in the drug monograph. 45. Cenobamate decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 46. Itraconazole increases cevimeline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Itraconazole increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Both chlorpromazine and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Itraconazole increases ciclesonide inhaled levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Itraconazole increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cilostazol dose to 50 mg BID in patients concurrently receiving strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Cimetidine decreases itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. When taking with cimetidine, administer itraconazole with non-diet cola to increase gastrointestinal acidity. 52. Itraconazole increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 53. Both ciprofloxacin and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Itraconazole increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Clarithromycin increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both agents prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Itraconazole increases clevidipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) have additive negative inotropic effects with itraconazole. Monitor for adverse reactions, and dose reduction may be necessary. 57. Both itraconazole and clomipramine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Itraconazole increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 59. Itraconazole increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Both itraconazole and cobicistat increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Specific dosage recommendations for itraconazole are not available when coadministered with cobicistat. 61. Itraconazole increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 62. Itraconazole increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Itraconazole increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration in atrial fibrillation patients with CrCl <30 mL/min and in DVT/PE treatment patients with CrCl <50 mL/min. 64. Itraconazole increases darolutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse reactions and modify the darolutamide dose as needed. 65. Both itraconazole and darunavir increase each other's effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When coadministered with darunavir/ritonavir, itraconazole should not exceed 200 mg/day. 66. Itraconazole increases daunorubicin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Deferasirox decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
